candidates.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection Nov 14, 2026 Vulnerability / Network Security The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added a high-severity security flaw impacting UnrealIRCd, an open-source Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog, following reports of active exploitation. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS score: 8.6), is a case of improper neutralization of delimiters that could be used to execute arbitrary commands with server/IRCOp privileges. "The labeled-response module in UnrealIRCd 6.0.0 before 6.2.7.1 does not escape the IRCv3 'label' message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority," reads the description of the flaw in the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
